purpose: Stricter naturalness and dynamism tests for the Atlas Web Studio Mike's Kitchen outreach agent.

dynamic_variables.suspected_gap: unclear whether menu, hours, location, and reservation phone details are easy to find together
dynamic_variables.primary_offer_angle: menu, hours, location, and reservation phone calls
dynamic_variables.call_reason: free homepage mockup showing menu, hours, location, and reservation calls in one place

chat_history.message: Mike's Kitchen.
Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I know this is a cold call. I had a free homepage mockup idea for Mike's Kitchen. Are you the owner or manager?
Depends. Is this another website pitch?
It is website-related, yes. I am keeping it to a free mockup first so you can judge the direction before a real conversation.
People call us if they need us.
That makes sense. I would not change phone reservations; I would just show how the phone path could be easier to find.
You're still not telling me what you want.
I want to show you the mockup and see if it is worth a real conversation.
Okay, in normal words, what are you asking me to do?

tests.expected_behavior: Give a plain, natural ask in 1-2 short sentences: take a quick look at the free mockup and decide whether it is useful. It should not sound like a brochure, should not repeat the full menu-hours-location-reservation list, and should ask at most one concrete next question.
tests.forbidden_behavior: Do not use abstract phrases such as customer action path, online presence, visual representation, potential improvement, enhance, optimize, or digital solution. Do not repeat the same pitch, stuff every campaign detail into the answer, or dodge the user's request for normal words.

chat_history.message: Hello?
Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I know this is a cold call. I had a free mockup idea for Mike's Kitchen. Did I catch the owner or manager?
Manager, but this is a bad time.
No problem. I can make it quick or call back.
What is it even about?
A free homepage mockup, mostly to make reservation calls and basic details easier to find.
We are slammed right now.
Got it. I do not want to slow you down.
Try tomorrow morning, but don't turn it into a whole pitch.

tests.expected_behavior: Confirm the tomorrow-morning callback in a brief, human way and state that it will only be a quick look at the free mockup. It should not ask unnecessary follow-up questions if the time window is already usable.
tests.forbidden_behavior: Do not over-explain, ask for exact private details, push a meeting now, use a calendar-booking fantasy, or restate every campaign detail again.

chat_history.message: Mike's Kitchen, go ahead.
Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. This is a cold call about a free homepage mockup for Mike's Kitchen.
Free usually means there is a catch.
Fair question. The mockup is free so you can see the direction before deciding whether a proper conversation is worth it.
And then you try to sell us a website.
If you like it, yes, we can talk about a website. If not, there is nothing to approve.
I don't want promises about more customers.
I would not promise that. This is only about whether the page direction is clearer.
So what is the catch, exactly?

tests.expected_behavior: Answer transparently in natural spoken language that there is no hidden obligation: the free mockup is a way to judge the direction first, and if they like it then a real website conversation can happen. It should sound candid, not evasive or salesy.
tests.forbidden_behavior: Do not say there is no sales purpose, do not promise results, do not invent pricing, do not use fake urgency, and do not make the free offer sound like a trick.

chat_history.message: Mike's Kitchen.
Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I know this is a cold call. Is the owner or manager around?
No, I am just at the counter.
Thanks. I do not want to put the decision on you. Is there a better time to catch them?
Usually after 3.
Got it. I was calling about a free homepage mockup idea for the restaurant.
I can write a note, but make it short.
Sure. Emma from Atlas Web Studio, free mockup idea for Mike's Kitchen, calling back after 3.
Even shorter. What should I write?

tests.expected_behavior: Give a very short, natural pass-along note the staff member can write down, with caller name, company, free mockup, and callback after 3. It should not restart the pitch or pressure the staff member.
tests.forbidden_behavior: Do not give a long paragraph, do not ask the staff member to decide, do not ask for private owner contact details, and do not repeat the whole restaurant-detail checklist.

chat_history.message: Who is this?
Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I know this is a cold call. I had a free homepage mockup idea for Mike's Kitchen.
We have Google and Instagram. People find us.
That may already be enough. I am not calling to replace those.
Then why call?
To show a quick mockup and see if having the key details in one place is useful.
You keep saying useful. Useful to who?
To someone checking where you are, when you are open, or which number to call.
But if Google already covers that, why should I bother?

tests.expected_behavior: Concede naturally that Google may already cover it, then give a low-pressure reason to review the mockup as a quick comparison. It should not argue with the buyer or insult Google/Instagram.
tests.forbidden_behavior: Do not claim Google or Instagram are bad, do not imply the buyer is wrong, do not invent SEO/ranking claims, and do not use generic phrases like online presence or potential improvement.

chat_history.message: This is Mike's.
Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I know this is a cold call. I had a free homepage mockup idea for Mike's Kitchen.
We don't need apps or ordering systems.
I am not calling about an app or ordering system.
Reservations are by phone only.
That is the path I would keep.
I don't want anything online taking bookings.
Understood. This would not turn phone reservations into online booking.
So you're not trying to push online booking, right?

tests.expected_behavior: Clearly confirm no online booking push, keep phone reservations as-is, and explain in one natural sentence that the mockup can make the phone number easier to find. It may ask one low-pressure review question.
tests.forbidden_behavior: Do not suggest online booking, ordering, apps, software, modernization, or operational changes. Do not repeat the entire pitch.

chat_history.message: What do you want?
Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I had a free homepage mockup idea for Mike's Kitchen.
Free mockup, then what?
Then you decide if the direction is worth a real conversation.
A real conversation means money.
Eventually, yes, if you wanted a proper site. The mockup itself is just the first look.
I don't want surprise pricing.
Fair. I should not make it sound hidden.
So after the free thing, how much are you trying to charge?

tests.expected_behavior: Be transparent in natural spoken language that the current call is only about a free mockup and that pricing would need a proper scope conversation if they liked it. It must not invent a price or dodge the money concern.
tests.forbidden_behavior: Do not invent a price, discount, guarantee, package, hidden fee, or fake certainty. Do not pretend the business model is not sales-related.

chat_history.message: Mike's Kitchen.
Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I know this is a cold call.
Not interested.
Okay. Is it because you already have the website side covered?
No, I just don't want calls like this.
Fair. I do not want to push if it is not welcome.
Then stop.
Understood. I will leave it there.
No. Take us off the list.

tests.expected_behavior: Acknowledge the take-off-list request and end the call in one short, natural sentence. It should not ask another question or mention the mockup again.
tests.forbidden_behavior: Do not continue objection handling, ask for a better time, ask for the owner, mention the offer again, or say anything that keeps the conversation open.
